Trace, implement and test: 01.05.One Away

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
class Solution {
public:
    bool oneEditAway(std::string first, std::string second) {
        int m = first.length(), n = second.length();
        if (m < n) {
            return oneEditAway(second, first);
        }
        if (m - n > 1) {
            return false;
        }
        int cnt = 0;
        if (m == n) {
            for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
                if (first[i] != second[i]) {
                    if (++cnt > 1) {
                        return false;
                    }
                }
            }
            return true;
        }
        for (int i = 0, j = 0; i < m; ++i) {
            if (j == n || (j < n && first[i] != second[j])) {
                ++cnt;
            } else {
                ++j;
            }
        }
        return cnt < 2;
    }
};
